question.problem: Find the perimeter of a square whose diagonal is $\frac{48}{\sqrt{2}}\,mm.$
question.worked_solution:
A diagram of the given situation is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182820/assets/5844e63004f2c12f7af15b2fe178a3e48f67e63d06692db532e5261d3f9f7df6.png)

Notice that $△FHG$ is a ${45}^{∘}$-${45}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle since $HG=GF$ and $m∠HGF={90}^{∘}.$

The hypotenuse in an isosceles right triangle is equal to $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of a leg. 

Here, the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{FH}$ is $\frac{48}{\sqrt{2}}\,mm.$ So the length of the leg $\overset{―}{HG}$ can be found by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}FH & =\sqrt{2}\cdot HG \\ \frac{48}{\sqrt{2}} & =\sqrt{2}\cdot HG \\ HG & =\frac{48}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\ HG & =\frac{48}{2} \\ HG & =24\,mm\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the perimeter $p$ is given by

$$
p=4\cdot HG=4\cdot 24=96\,mm.
$$
